messages:
hana: FYI — ACME reporting service-principal tokens started getting 403s to /v1/models/gpt-4x after last night's RBAC refactor. Works in console, fails from CI.
acme-ops: Repro steps from our CI:
```
curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer sp|XXXX' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/gpt-4x/invoke -d '{"input":"hi"}'
=> 403 {"error":"forbidden","detail":"missing permission: models.invoke"}
```
Weirdly the same token used for other API calls (billing, embeddings) works.
sanjay: @hana assigning to eng-security. That pattern smells like scope truncation or mapping bug. We recently changed role->scope storage (packed CSV into varchar(1024)).
aj: I'll grep the auth service and DB migration logs now.
kim: ops-bot shows KMS unwraps success; token issuance logs show scopes payload length 1765 chars for that token.
ops-bot: TokenIssue event recorded for tenant=acme-corp, token_id=sp|XXXX, scopes_length=1765, issued_by=svc-deploy
sanjay: Interesting — issuance audit has full scopes, but the policy check returns a smaller set. Hypothesis: scopes truncated when saved to permissions table or during in-memory split.
aj: Found it in services/authz/handler.go:
```
// legacy truncate to prevent really long values
if len(saveScopes) > 1024 {
    saveScopes = saveScopes[:1024]
}
```
Looks like legacy guard left in after refactor.
marta: Customer impact: blocked CI and delayed deploys for 2 teams at ACME. They want ETA and mitigations.
sanjay: Plan: hotfix the truncation (remove the slice), change column type to TEXT in a safe migration, add unit tests, and canary deploy to prod region. Also plan a short-lived fallback mapping for affected tenants to unblock before full rollout.
hana: Deploy plan outline:
- create hotfix PR -> test in staging with synthetic token containing 2000+ char scope list
- if pass, canary to 5% traffic for 30m
- full rollout with 2h maintenance window if stable
- rotate affected tokens post-deploy
@acme-ops we'll coordinate timing.
acme-ops: Thanks — we can rotate tokens after you give a 30m heads-up. We prefer rotation during our off-peak window (02:00 UTC).
kim: Temporary mitigation applied: mapped sp|XXXX to fallback role "models-invoke" for tenant acme-corp to unblock builds. This is a short-lived change and logged in audit (action=manual_role_map, actor=kim).
sanjay: Hotfix PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/4827 — removing truncation and adding tests. DB migration ticket: INFRA-1299.
ops-bot: Deploy started: infra-hotfix/v1.3.5 -> staging
aj: Staging verification: created token with scopes length 2200, invoked model endpoint, accepted 200 OK and response returned. No permission errors.
ops-bot: Canary promoted to prod-5pct -> success metrics within SLOs.
sanjay: Rolled to prod. Post-deploy smoke: tokens re-evaluated, and ACME CI jobs now pass end-to-end. Recommend rotation of affected tokens once ACME ready.
marta: Communicating to customer: sent DM and emailed incident summary + remediation steps. Will schedule rotation with ACME.
acme-ops: Confirmed — CI green. Please rotate tokens at 02:00 UTC tomorrow. Thanks team :thumbsup:
sanjay: Postmortem TO-DOs: root cause = leftover truncation guard on scope save (varchar(1024)). Actions: 1) DB migration to TEXT (INFRA-1299), 2) add unit/regression test for long scope lists, 3) add lint to catch slice truncations, 4) audit export for affected tenant (done), 5) update RBAC docs about maximum scope lengths (now unlimited).
hana: Closing loop: ACME confirmed access restored and CI passing. We'll keep the temporary fallback mapping until tokens rotated. I'll open the postmortem doc and assign owners.
aj: Assigned INFRA-1299 to me. Will land migration next week with zero-downtime steps.
kim: Marked incident resolved in incident tracker. Follow-up: we'll run a quick sweep for other places that might have similar legacy truncates.
marta: Customer happy, closing escalation. Thanks everyone.
